title: NVIDIA Vera Rubin and Blackwell Set a New Standard for Agentic AI Performance per Watt | NVIDIA Technical Blog
gist: NVIDIA reports preview results on SemiAnalysis AgentX — a benchmark that replays recorded Claude Code sessions rather than fixed-length prompts — claiming Vera Rubin NVL72 delivers up to 30x higher throughput per megawatt than GB300 NVL72 at 160 tokens/sec/user, and GB300 up to 15x over H200 NVL8 rising to ~80x on Kimi K3 2.8T. The Vera Rubin numbers are NVIDIA-measured and pending SemiAnalysis review, and the static 8K/1K sequence-length benchmark has been demoted to maintenance mode as unrepresentative of agentic traffic.

insights.claim: Across 100 trillion tokens of real-world usage, OpenRouter's State of AI report found average prompt tokens per request grew roughly fourfold and a single agentic request consumes 15 times the tokens of an ordinary chat request.
insights.speaker: Jamie Li
insights.so_what: The clearest demand-side number in the piece: agentic adoption multiplies inference token volume ~15x per request, which is the mechanism converting agent adoption into datacenter capex.
insights.quote: average prompt tokens per request grew roughly fourfold, and single agentic requests consume 15 times the tokens of ordinary chat
insights.locator: AI agents have expanded inference from single-turn interactions

insights.claim: Agentic inference is characterized by long-context prefill, KV-cache reuse, interactive decode, tool-call gaps and distributed MoE execution under realistic concurrency — a materially different workload profile from the single-turn chat inference that current hardware was benchmarked on.
insights.speaker: Jamie Li
insights.so_what: Five workload attributes to check against any inference hardware claim; a vendor benchmarking on fixed-length chat is answering last year's question.
insights.locator: Properly characterizing hardware performance for this workload

insights.claim: AgentX measures serving performance by replaying prerecorded Claude Code sessions turn by turn through the AIPerf client, preserving each session's context, sequence lengths, reasoning time and tool-call latency so KV-cache capacity pressure is reproduced.
insights.speaker: Jamie Li
insights.so_what: Trace-replay benchmarking makes vendor tuning harder to hide; expect procurement to migrate toward it and away from synthetic sequence-length tests.
insights.quote: Because every system receives the same recorded traffic, observed differences reflect the serving stack rather than benchmark-specific tuning.
insights.locator: AgentX addresses that gap by measuring serving performance

insights.claim: The legacy fixed 8K input / 1K output sequence-length scenario has been demoted to maintenance mode on the InferenceX suite because it no longer represents production traffic — an explicit obsolescence of the benchmark format most inference comparisons still use.
insights.speaker: Jamie Li
insights.so_what: Any competitive inference claim still quoted on 8K/1K should be discounted; the goalposts for hardware comparison have formally moved.
insights.quote: a fixed sequence length scenario has become less representative of true serving performance and has been demoted to “maintenance mode” on the InferenceX suite
insights.locator: In real agent sessions, request lengths vary from turn to turn.

insights.claim: The metric that matters for AI factories is tokens per megawatt, reported against four user-experience axes — E2E normalized interactivity, standard interactivity, E2E latency, and time to first token — because high efficiency is worthless if requests take too long to finish.
insights.speaker: Jamie Li
insights.so_what: Perf-per-watt quoted without an interactivity target is meaningless; always ask at what tokens/sec/user the efficiency number was measured.
insights.quote: high efficiency does not help if requests take too long to finish

insights.claim: At 160 tokens per second per user on the AgentX DeepSeek V4-Pro workload, Vera Rubin NVL72 is claimed to deliver up to 30x higher AI-factory throughput per megawatt than GB300 NVL72.
insights.speaker: Jamie Li
insights.so_what: A 30x generational efficiency jump, if it holds, resets the depreciation math on Blackwell-era capacity and pulls forward Rubin upgrade demand.
insights.quote: at 160 tokens per second per user on the AgentX DeepSeek V4-Pro workload, Vera Rubin NVL72 delivers up to 30x higher AI-factory throughput per megawatt than GB300 NVL72

insights.claim: The Vera Rubin NVL72 figures were measured by NVIDIA itself using the AgentX workload and are explicitly pending SemiAnalysis review — self-reported preview numbers, not independently validated results.
insights.speaker: Jamie Li
insights.so_what: The single most important caveat in the piece: hold the 30x claim provisionally until SemiAnalysis publishes verified results on its InferenceX dashboard.
insights.quote: The following Vera Rubin NVL72 results were measured by NVIDIA using the SemiAnalysis AgentX workload and are pending SemiAnalysis review.

insights.claim: On AgentX, GB300 NVL72 delivers up to 15x higher throughput per megawatt than H200 NVL8 for DeepSeek V4 Pro 1.6T, and up to 10x lower cost per million tokens.
insights.speaker: Jamie Li
insights.so_what: A 10x token-cost delta between Hopper and Blackwell racks means H200-based inference fleets are structurally uncompetitive on unit economics — accelerating fleet turnover and residual-value decay.
insights.quote: GB300 NVL72 delivers up to 10x lower cost per million tokens than H200 NVL8 (Figure 6, below).

insights.claim: The generational advantage widens with model scale — from 15x on a 1.6T model to roughly 80x on Kimi K3 2.8T, where GB300 NVL72 also extends the interactivity frontier to about 215 tokens per second per user, beyond H200 NVL8's operating range.
insights.speaker: Jamie Li
insights.so_what: Frontier-model scaling is self-reinforcing for rack-scale NVLink systems: the larger the MoE, the wider the moat versus 8-GPU nodes and merchant alternatives.
insights.quote: With roughly 80x the throughput per megawatt of H200 NVL8 at comparable interactivity, GB300 NVL72 also extends the interactivity frontier to roughly 215 tokens per second per user, well beyond the operating range reached by H200 NVL8.
insights.locator: The advantage of GB300 NVL72 becomes more pronounced

insights.claim: On the legacy static 8K/1K DeepSeek-R1-0528 test, GB300 NVL72 led H200 by up to 40x more tokens per megawatt — a higher headline multiple than the 15x it posts on realistic agentic traffic for a comparable model.
insights.speaker: Jamie Li
insights.so_what: Realistic agentic replay compresses the generational gap versus synthetic tests — evidence that published perf-per-watt multiples flatter newer hardware.
insights.quote: GB300 NVL72 leads H200 by up to 40x more tokens per megawatt.

themes.theme: Where the gains actually come from

insights.claim: NVIDIA attributes the GB300 results to system-level software work as much as silicon — MoE serving runtimes SGLang, TensorRT-LLM and vLLM distributing expert execution across the NVL72 domain via Wide Expert Parallelism and DeepEP to raise effective batch size.
insights.speaker: Jamie Li
insights.so_what: Several of these runtimes and techniques are open source and not NVIDIA-owned, meaning a portion of the claimed advantage is portable to competing accelerators once ported.

insights.claim: Kernel-level gains come from DeepGEMM-based kernels, MXFP4 and MXFP8 mixed-precision formats, and fused MoE execution paths that overlap expert-parallel communication with Tensor Core computation.
insights.speaker: Jamie Li
insights.so_what: Sub-8-bit mixed-precision formats are now load-bearing for headline efficiency numbers — a reminder that perf-per-watt gains are partly precision reductions, not pure hardware.

insights.claim: NVIDIA Dynamo separates prefill and decode into independently scaled worker pools and adds session-aware serving through session IDs correlating model calls, tool spans and traces across an agent run, with a KV-cache-aware router selecting workers by cache overlap and load to avoid redundant prefill.
insights.speaker: Jamie Li
insights.so_what: Cache-aware routing turns context reuse into a direct cost saving; it is the software layer where inference margin is won, and a reason serving-stack ownership matters more than raw FLOPs.
insights.quote: its KV-cache-aware router uses cache overlap and worker load to select a target, reducing unnecessary prefill computation

insights.claim: The NVLink scale-up fabric connecting all 72 GPUs as one high-bandwidth domain is what makes rack-scale expert-parallel communication and KV-cache movement viable for large MoE models.
insights.speaker: Jamie Li
insights.so_what: The 72-GPU coherent domain is the structural advantage competitors must replicate; scale-up fabric, not the GPU die, is the harder thing to copy.

insights.claim: NVIDIA's forward architecture splits the agentic workflow across specialized processors: Rubin GPUs for large context and decode, Vera CPUs for tool execution and KV-cache offload, and Groq 3 LPX for ultrafast interactivity.
insights.speaker: Jamie Li
insights.so_what: The unit of sale is shifting from GPU to heterogeneous rack complex — raising dollar content per deployment and making single-component competition harder to mount.
insights.quote: Rubin GPUs process large context and decode efficiently, Vera CPUs handle tool execution and KV-cache offload, and Groq 3 LPX unlocks ultrafast interactivity.

insights.claim: NVLink 6, ConnectX-9, BlueField-4 and Spectrum-X are positioned as the movement layer for tokens, context and tool results between these resources, with Dynamo, Attention-FFN Disaggregation, NVFP4, TensorRT-LLM WideEP and speculative decoding coordinating execution across processors.
insights.speaker: Jamie Li
insights.so_what: A full component checklist for the Rubin-era rack — each named part is an NVIDIA-branded revenue line displacing a formerly merchant or open component.
insights.locator: Across the AI factory, NVLink 6, ConnectX-9

insights.claim: The stated design objective is to convert more of a fixed power budget into useful agentic output by reducing recomputation and waiting — an explicit acknowledgment that power, not capital, is the binding constraint on AI factory scaling.
insights.speaker: Jamie Li
insights.so_what: If megawatts are the scarce input, perf-per-watt gains translate directly into incremental sellable capacity — which is why utility and grid access increasingly gate datacenter operator valuations.
